In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation criteria used by pharmacy schools in making promotion and tenure (P&T) decisions.
the relative importance of the various criteria that are used to evaluate faculty members when making decisions about promotion and tenure.
the relative importance of the various performance criteria that are currently being used to make promotion and tenure decisions in U.S. pharmacy schools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative importance of performance criteria in promotion and tenure decisions varies by institution.

the relative importance of performance criteria in promotion and tenure decisions varies widely among pharmacy faculty members and among the institutions in which they work, and that the criteria that are most important to pharmacy faculty members are those that they themselves believe they can best influence.

the relative importance of various performance criteria for promotion and tenure decisions is a function of the individual faculty member, the institution, the department, and the time period in which the decisions are being made.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need to improve the current system of promotion and tenure in pharmacy education.

there is a need for a more systematic approach to promotion and tenure decisions that would include a more comprehensive set of criteria and a more systematic process for collecting evidence of performance on each of those criteria.

we have found a number of areas where there are discrepancies between the current and preferred importance of evaluation criteria, which should be considered when evaluating faculty members for promotion and tenure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the criteria that are currently being used to make promotion and tenure decisions may not reflect the criteria that faculty members feel are most important.
there are differences between what is currently being done and what faculty members believe should be done.
there is an important need to improve the promotion and tenure process in order to ensure that it reflects the best interests of the profession, the institutions, and the faculty members themselves.
